goal: Reduce the source's diagnostic maximum-rank summed NCCL kernel duration for the accumulated training step, retaining its step-time constraint and full correctness checks.
completion: The measured invocation is one full accumulated DDP training step (gpt2_ddp_training.py step(), lines 102-105): optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True), then accumulation_steps forward/backward microbatches of micro_batch x sequence_length tokens each under DDP with no_sync() on all but the last microbatch and one gradient all-reduce on the final microbatch, then optimizer.step(), ending at the source's internal torch.cuda.synchronize() completion boundary. The step consumes world_size x micro_batch x sequence_length x accumulation_steps = 1024 tokens with effective batch 8. Harness work surrounding it (reference construction, gradient/parameter checks, exact replica broadcast, negative control, the separate bucket-inventory comm-hook run, the 3 profiled diagnostic runs, report writing) is not part of the invocation.
state_protocol: prepare() configures the source's numerical policy on context['device'], builds the seeded FP32 GPT-2 (torch.manual_seed(20261020)), wraps it in DDP(broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True), creates SGD(lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False), synthesizes per-rank token inputs (generator seed 31000 + source_rank) and snapshots initial weights to CPU. reset() restores those initial weights via raw_model.load_state_dict(initial) outside timing, mirroring the source's reset() (gpt2_ddp_training.py:99-100); gradient clearing is NOT moved into reset because the source performs optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) inside the timed accumulate() (gpt2_ddp_training.py:37). before_run() reproduces the source's pre-step control-group barrier plus CUDA sync outside the timer. run() repeats the identical step from the restored start state each invocation (the 4 accumulation iterations are genuine internal work). The worker-initialized process group is never destroyed and no second default group is created; a gloo control subgroup is created only for coordination. observe() runs outside timing, clones loss, all gradients and updated parameters to CPU, and performs the exact cross-rank gradient broadcast check. metrics() queries CUDA peak statistics outside the timer.
invariants: Numerical policy is frozen by the request notes: FP32 weights, TF32 disabled for CUDA matmul and cudnn, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'), cudnn.benchmark False (common.py configure; request notes preserve precision).

Model architecture is frozen by the request: GPT-2 with n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, vocab_size=50257, n_positions=1024, resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.0, use_cache=False, eager attention (workloads.json gpt2_ddp_training.model; request forbids changing model architecture).

Workload dimensions are read from request['workload'] (world_size=2, micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128, accumulation_steps=4; effective batch 8; 1024 tokens per step) and must not be reduced or altered (request freezes batch, sequence length, effective training batch and work amount).

Task data are the source's declared seeded synthetic fixtures: weight initialization manual_seed(20261020) and per-source-rank token generator seed 31000 + source_rank with values in [0, vocab_size) (gpt2_ddp_training.py make_model/make_inputs; request notes declare these valid task data; assets is legitimately empty).

run() must execute the entire frozen workload: full gradient accumulation over all accumulation_steps microbatches, the required NCCL gradient all-reduce on the last microbatch, the SGD optimizer update, and the source's synchronize boundary (request: a training workload must include the full accumulation, required communication and optimizer update).

optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) stays inside the timed invocation rather than being pre-cleared in reset(), because the source executes it within accumulate() on every step (gpt2_ddp_training.py:37); the source's setup/timed division must be preserved.

Exact discrete correctness checks are required in observe(), outside timed run(), because per-rank tolerance comparisons cannot enforce participant relationships: every parameter gradient must be identical across ranks via broadcast and assert_close(atol=0.0, rtol=0.0) (exact_gradient_replica_check, gpt2_ddp_training.py:81-86), the negative control must reject +1-corrupted gradients, and the training loss must be finite (request notes).

Reference fidelity uses the request's quality tolerances (grad_atol/parameter_atol 1e-06, grad_rtol/parameter_rtol 1e-04) against the serial single-GPU accumulation of the exact same global batch plus the post-step parameter comparison; the adapter must reproduce the source's full gradients, loss and updated parameters as observations so this check remains meaningful (request quality and notes; no accuracy or convergence claim beyond reference fidelity).

The step-time constraint step_ms <= 1.05x baseline (max across ranks of one full accumulated step's local wall time) applies to the full request; communication improvements may not trade away step time or the unchanged work amount (request objective.constraints).

The frozen objective communication_kernel_sum_ms is collected by the framework's torch_communication collector in separate diagnostic runs; the adapter must not fabricate, inline or approximate it inside run()/metrics() (request objective.source).
assumptions: Model dimensions are embedded as frozen architecture constants taken from workloads.json gpt2_ddp_training.model, because request['workload'] carries only workload-dependent dimensions; a separately validated workload variant (e.g. held-out longer_sequence with sequence_length 256, accumulation_steps 2) changes only workload fields through the same request structure while the architecture stays fixed.

The rank-0 serial global-batch reference, its gradient/parameter comparisons and negative-control scaffolding in the source are measurement and quality infrastructure surrounding the invocation; the framework stores reference observations on CPU, so this adapter does not allocate a second reference model on GPU. The baseline reproduces the source's exact gradient, loss and parameter values, which is what those comparisons verify.

The separate bucket-inventory comm-hook run and the 3 profiled diagnostic runs (median-of-3 max-rank NCCL kernel sum) are diagnostics owned by the framework; the baseline registers no communication hook and runs no profiler inside run()/metrics().

DDP reducer options (broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True), SGD hyperparameters (lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False) and no_sync() on the first accumulation_steps-1 microbatches are the source baseline's implementation choices reproduced faithfully here; they remain legitimate optimization surfaces as long as the exact cross-rank gradient check, the reference-fidelity tolerances and the step-time constraint still hold.

The source's gloo control group exists only for timing barriers; the adapter reproduces that coordination in before_run() (CUDA sync plus barrier) without re-initializing or destroying the worker's process group, falling back to the default group if gloo subgroup creation fails.

set_mode() only records the mode because the source has no separate correctness-capture path: execution semantics, work amount and observations are identical in quality, measure and profile modes; kernel_optimizer.project.discovery.phase annotations are labels only and add no work.

metrics() exposes the source's clean project metrics (step_ms, tokens_per_second, peak_allocated_bytes, loss, parameter_count, effective_batch, tokens_per_step) in native units; step_ms is the local wall time whose max across ranks is the constraint metric, and the communication objective is left to the framework's collector.
The held-out workload longer_sequence is not part of this frozen request and is not exercised; request['assets'] is empty by design because the entry never reads --assets.
